A_target.statement:
A [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] $M$ is an [[Definition:Topological Manifold|$n$-manifold]] if every point has a [[Definition:Neighborhood (Topology)|neighborhood]] [[Definition:Homeomorphic|homeomorphic]] to an [[Definition:Open Set (Real Analysis)|open subset]] of $\R^n$.
Such $M$ carries [[Definition:Chart|charts]], [[Definition:Transition Map|transition maps]] and a notion of [[Definition:Orientable Manifold|orientability]].

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] $S$ is a [[Definition:Surface|surface]] if every point has a [[Definition:Neighborhood (Topology)|neighborhood]] [[Definition:Homeomorphic|homeomorphic]] to an [[Definition:Open Set (Real Analysis)|open subset]] of $\R^2$.

substitutions.the plane as the local model: n-dimensional Euclidean space as the local model
substitutions.charts onto planar regions: charts onto open subsets of R^n

derived.the atlas and its transition maps: the same notions in n dimensions
derived.orientability via consistent chart orien: orientability via positive determinants of transition Jacobians

object_map.reformulation: Raise the dimension of the local model, keeping the chart-and-atlas definition unchanged.

validity_conditions: Surfaces are the case n equal to two, so every n-dimensional notion specializes correctly and the generalization is faithful.
The local definition is dimension-agnostic, so charts, atlases, and transition maps transfer with no change beyond the number of coordinates.

Classification does not transfer: closed surfaces are classified completely, whereas in dimension four no such classification exists, so the generalization is of the definitions rather than the structure theory.
proof_plan: Replace $\R^2$ by $\R^n$ as the local model.

Define a [[Definition:Chart|chart]] as a homeomorphism $\phi: U \to \map \phi U \subseteq \R^n$, an [[Definition:Atlas|atlas]] as a family of charts covering $M$, and [[Definition:Transition Map|transition maps]] $\phi_\beta \circ \phi_\alpha^{-1}$ in $n$ coordinates.

$M$ is [[Definition:Smooth Manifold|smooth]] if all transition maps are smooth, and [[Definition:Orientable Manifold|orientable]] if there is an atlas whose transition [[Definition:Jacobian Determinant|Jacobians]] are everywhere positive.
